newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market closed lower on Wednesday dragged lower by weak Italian Btps, despite optimistic expectations for February CPI.
"The CPI will be good, but it seems that this is something the market has already discounted," a dealer in Madrid said.

February CPI is seen falling to around 2.7/2.8 percent year-on-year from 2.9 percent in January. Analysts are mixed on the possibility that good data will prompt the Bank of Spain to cut its six percent key money market rate.
"I don't think this is the right time, the markets are too volatile," a dealer added.
The 10-year spread over Bunds widened to around 133 bps versus 130 bps, while Spain's yield curve flattened a bit.
Six-month bill yields, which were unchanged, were also considered proof that the "market was not really expecting a rate cut on Friday," dealers said.
